source.original_title: 05/16/2026 - Mustafa Jibawi & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/16/2026 - Mustafa Jibawi & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'know you spoke with Kim, he, uh, kind of gave me a head start on you.' Prospect, unprompted at 01:10:48: 'I appreciate how persistent Kim has been'. Prospect also referenced telling Kim about his first week on Trevor's content and about the nutrition programme he was already paying for. Note the rep refers to Kim as 'he'.

prospect.name: Mustafa Jibawi
prospect.location: Denver, Colorado, USA (Mountain Time); born and raised in Chicago
prospect.occupation: Flight attendant for a US airline, returning to full-time flying the week of the call. Had been working a second part-time job in property management in Denver; his last day there was the day before this call.
prospect.training_background: Peaked at 220 lb, lost 60-70 lb on keto down to roughly 175 lb following Thomas DeLauer's content, then came off keto after about eighteen months when his sleep and stress deteriorated, and regained about half over several years. Long history of weight lifting which left him stiff. Has trained with Trevor's free online content for one week before this call and reported a noticeable posture change. Owns one 15 lb kettlebell and has a 20 lb set on order, due in three or four days.
prospect.medical: Hip injury limiting how hard he can train. Seen by his primary doctor and chiropractors; he cannot recall the diagnosis name but has the paperwork. Assessed as minor — no MRI or x-ray ordered, no surgery discussed — and he has been assigned physical therapy, which is ongoing. He and his clinicians believe it is muscular and fixable. Also reports waking unrefreshed, 'like I've gotten hit by a bus', with low energy and disrupted sleep, partly attributed to cross-time-zone work.

signals: Had the result and lost it: down to 175 lb on keto, back to 198 lb, and wants that version of himself back
Explicit age-identity regret: 'I just want to feel like I'm 34, not like I'm 50, you know, like, I'm only 34'

Tension in the assignment: he frames the belly fat as lifelong rather than lost ground — 'lose weight that I just have never been able to lose. In my 34 years' — which pulls toward a rescue profile rather than a rebuild
Not skeptical_bargain_hunter despite the $200/month anchor: the cheap alternative did NOT work for him, he calls it a scam, so the anchor is a trust wound rather than a functioning substitute

goals.text: Feel better in his body and have vitality — 'I just want to feel healthier'
Lose the stubborn belly fat he has never been able to shift
Get rid of the hip pain that limits how hard he can train
Do it without laborious macro counting or a mathematical equation at every meal
Feel his actual age rather than fifty, and stop talking with friends about getting old
Be well in his body the way Trevor appears to be — 'he just seems like he's just well in his body'

pains.text: Stubborn belly fat resistant to every diet he has tried across 34 years
Hip injury under active physical therapy that stops him pushing or training as much as he wants
Flight attendant schedule changes every week with no fixed days, and layover hotel gyms rarely have kettlebells
Wakes feeling hit by a bus with low energy and no sleep structure, worsened by crossing time zones
Currently six weeks into a $200/month nutrition programme he believes is a scam — one body scan, five-minute weekly calls, and processed protein bars and chips he does not want to eat
Keto worked then broke him: 'my body was like, this is way too stressful for me. I can't do this anymore. I wasn't sleeping well'
Financial strain — has needed two jobs to get by and a $6,000 outlay feels like being forced back to a second job
Fear of success surfaced unprompted: reaching the goal feels 'bittersweet, but probably more bitter than sweet' because he does not know what comes after

objections.raw_quote: I just, I can't justify 6k, especially in my current financial situation. Um, I mean, I thought $600 across three months was a lot for a nutritional program, right?
objections.rep_response: Isolated it — 'money aside, do you feel as though you're a hundred percent confident that you'll get where you want to go with it' — got an unqualified yes, ran a worth-it hypothetical, then a perspective reframe about the two ways to interpret a pay rise. Later moved to the should-I versus how-do-I frame and offered payment structures.

objections.raw_quote: with a pay increase, I can finally go back to just one job, and spending 6k makes me feel like I have to go back to a second job again, and I just can't do that, you know what I mean
objections.rep_response: Reframed rather than tested. Argued that the only true facts are the pay rise and the $6,000 and that everything else is meaning we assign, then characterised his caution as a scarcity pattern: 'it's always been a scarce thing for you.' Did not ask for any actual figure — no income, no surplus, no cash on hand. Later offered a 12-month plan costing more.

objections.raw_quote: the better part of me now is saying don't make the decision right here right now just like you did with the nutritional program um you need to take what you've gotten from this conversation take a step back actually work out my finances
objections.rep_response: Interjected and mapped the hesitation onto the two fears he had pre-framed twenty minutes earlier, then argued the nutrition purchase was not a bad decision. Followed with 'If you knew you couldn't fail, would you do it?' and the God-in-the-Zoom-chat hypothetical, then 'are you going to look for reasons why you should do it or reasons why you shouldn't do it?'. Eventually conceded the 24 hours and booked a follow-up.

Normalised it — 'It's good to be nervous. It means, uh, if you weren't nervous, then it probably wouldn't be a good thing for you.' Earlier he had pre-framed both the fear of success and the fear of repeating the nutritionist mistake, using a skydiving image and a falling-off-a-bike image.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two routes given. Internal: 50% upfront and the balance within 90 days, which keeps the total at $6,000 — 'anything after that internally is, like, has extra added on'. Instalment: $650 a month for 12 months, described only as adding 'a little bit extra' with interest removable on early payoff. The $7,800 total was never stated. Klarna was also offered and a live soft credit check was run on a Stripe link during the call; it returned declined twice. The prospect said he would lean toward the $650 a month option.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: 'The guarantee is that in six months, with every single kettlebell movement... you will be doing every movement with 18, eight kilo kettlebell or 18 pounds heavier by the end of it... if you're not there, and you've done everything, we will just work with you until you're at that point anyway.' Offered explicitly as the answer to what expectations he should set.

prospect_financials.note: Disclosed that he has needed two jobs to get by, that a pay rise had just kicked in two weeks earlier, that he quit the second job the day before and does not yet know what his finances look like on one income, and that $600 over three months already felt like a lot. No income figure, cash-on-hand figure, monthly surplus or available credit was ever requested.

evidence: Explicit and repeated request for time: 'Harry, I, I would like to sit with this... I need a set amount of time to actually think about it. Whether that's 24 hours, 36 hours' and later 'I wouldn't need more than 24 hours to think this through'
No verbal agreement to proceed at any point; the closest is a statement of intent to look for reasons to make it work — 'I'm going to look for reasons for why I need to do this'

A Stripe link was sent, but explicitly not as a purchase: 'You don't have to do it now. Like I'm not asking you to pay when I do this. I just want to see if this is an option so you can take it with you... This isn't you signing up for anything.' The verbal-agreement-plus-link-sent rule therefore does not apply
Klarna returned declined twice on a soft check, removing the instalment route he was leaning toward

Positive counter-evidence: a follow-up Zoom was booked live for noon Mountain the next day, WhatsApp numbers exchanged, and he confirmed strong belief in the programme — 'Yes, I have no doubt... I feel pretty confident about what you stand for'
outcome.next_step: Follow-up Zoom booked for noon Mountain the following day, on the rep's day off. Prospect to work through his finances on his day off and decide within 24 hours. Rep to send the calendar link and connect on WhatsApp; prospect also to investigate why Klarna declined him.

notable.note: The instalment route quoted here is $650 a month for twelve months. That is $7,800 — $1,800 above the $6,000 six-month price — and the total was never spoken aloud on the call. The uplift was characterised as 'a little bit extra'. The prospect, who had just told the rep that $6,000 would force him back to the second job he had quit the day before, said he would lean toward exactly this option. Separately, the rep asked whether the prospect believed in God and then built a closing hypothetical around God endorsing the purchase in the Zoom chat, and ran a live Klarna credit application minutes after the prospect said he needed to step back and avoid another rash decision. On the credit side, this is by a wide margin the best-run baseline and past-attempts work in the batch, the fear-of-success exploration at 00:24:34 is the deepest discovery moment in the corpus so far, and the rep pre-framed both objections twenty minutes before they landed.

quality.notes: Extensive inversion throughout, worst in the second half. The entire offer walkthrough from roughly 00:30:27 to 00:40:24 is split near-randomly between the two labels while being almost entirely the rep. The guarantee explanation at 00:40:52 to 00:43:08 is attributed largely to 'Mustafa Jibawi' but is the rep. The payment-plan mechanics at 01:05:11 to 01:06:40 alternate wrongly. The opening also mislabels which speaker is in Denver and which is in London. Roles read from content throughout.
